$comment: Canonical record of the Beagle contract snapshot Walker is built against, and the drift baseline. On any future AUTHORIZED re-sync, recompute each Beagle source artifact's SHA-256 and compare to `sha256` below: a changed checksum means the contract changed -> re-sync -> re-record SHA -> re-run contract tests -> adjust implementation if needed. This manifest is also how a re-sync knows exactly which files to pull and from where (note the integration contract's source path is one level up from the other three).

beagle.authority: Beagle is the canonical contract authority. These copies are read-only consumption artifacts, not an independent source of truth. Walker never edits, commits, branches, or pushes to Beagle, and never edits these local copies to resolve a disagreement — discrepancies are reported to Beagle to fix at the authority.
